cards.narration: This is Pip the frog. Pip loves to count. Today he hops on stones.
Here are 3 stones. Pip counts 1, 2, 3. We count by ones.
Hop one more. After 3 comes 4. After 4 comes 5.
Pip can start anywhere. Now he starts at 7. Next is 8, then 9.
Keep going! 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Each stone is one more.
Pip hops on. 16, 17, 18, 19, 20! He counted to 20.
Now you count with Pip. Are you ready?
Meet Mia. Mia loves numbers. Numbers help us in three ways. Let's find them!
Mia has 3 apples. The number 3 means how many. We can count them.
Now 5 ducks stand in a line. Numbers can tell which one. This duck is first.
The next duck is second. Then comes third. First, second, third show the place in line.
Mia has a team shirt. It has the number 24. Here, the number is a name.
So numbers can mean how many. They can mean which one. And they can be a name.
cards.text: how many, which one, a name

cards.narration: Now you try! Mia will help you find how numbers are used.
This is Mia. Mia has 2 ladybugs. Look fast! You can see 2.
Now Mia has 3 ladybugs. Look fast! You do not need to count. It is 3.
Mia finds 4 ladybugs. Two and two make 4. Look fast!
Here is 1 ladybug. One is easy to see.
Here are 5 dots on a ten-frame. The dots fill one whole row. That is 5!
Now you try! Look fast and find how many. Mia will help you.
Meet Pip the frog. Pip loves numbers! Let's count with Pip.
Pip sees apples. Count them. 1, 2, 3. There are 3 apples.
We use a number for 3. It looks like this. This is the number 3.
Now Pip sees dots in a box. Count them. There are 7 dots. The number is 7.
Oh! This box has no dots. No dots is 0. Zero means none.
Pip sees lots of stars. Count to 12. The number is 12.
You can match numbers to things. Ready to play with Pip?
Meet Pip the frog. Pip loves to count and hop!
Pip has a tower. Here are 3 blocks.
Pip adds one more block. Now there are 4. We counted up!
Pip adds one more. Now there are 5. Counting up makes the number bigger.
Now Pip takes one block away. There are 4. We counted down!
Pip takes one more away. Now there are 3. Counting down makes the number smaller.
Up gets bigger. Down gets smaller. Let's play with Pip!
Meet Pip the frog. Pip has 3 apples. Yum!
Mia is Pip's friend. Mia has 5 apples.
Mia has 5. Pip has 3. Mia has more apples than Pip.
Pip has fewer apples. 3 is less than 5.
Now Pip and Mia each have 4 apples. It is the same!
Now you try! Is it more, less, or the same? Hop in!
Meet Pip the frog. Pip has 3 apples.
Pip's friend has 5 apples. 5 is greater than 3. Greater means more.
3 is less than 5. Less means fewer. Pip has fewer apples.
Pip finds 1 more apple. Now Pip has 4. 1 more than 3 is 4.
Pip finds 2 more. 2 more than 5 is 7. Count up two.
Pip eats 1 apple. 1 less than 4 is 3. Count down one.
Now you try! Help Pip with more and less.
Meet Mia. She has 6 apples. Yum!
Mia puts 4 apples in a red basket.
2 apples are left. They go in a blue basket.
4 and 2 make 6. Six has two parts!
Now Mia has 5 pears. 3 are in a bag. How many are out? 2!
Let's practise! Find the parts of numbers.
Meet Pip the frog. Pip loves bugs. Pip loves to count them!
Pip sees 2 bugs on a leaf.
Then 3 more bugs come. Now Pip counts them all. 5 bugs!
2 and 3 make 5. Putting groups together is adding.
Now 2 bugs fly away. That is taking away. 3 bugs are left.
You can do it too. Let's play with Pip!
Meet Mia. She has 3 red apples.
Her friend gives her 2 more. Now she has 5 apples.
Mia has 8 apples. She gives 3 away. Now she has 5.
Here are 7 apples. 5 are red. The rest are green. 2 are green.
Ben has 4 apples. Mia has 8. Mia has 4 more than Ben.
Now let's practise with Mia! Use your fingers to help.
Mia has 6 yummy cookies. Her friend Sam comes to play.
Mia wants to share. Sharing equally means everyone gets the same.
One cookie for Mia. One cookie for Sam. Same for both!
Again! One more for Mia. One more for Sam. Now they each have 2.
One more each! Now all 6 cookies are shared. Each friend gets 3.
You can share fairly too. Let's play!

items.narration: Count with Pip. 1, 2, 3. What comes next? Is it 4, 7, or 2?
items.why: After 3 comes 4. We count by ones: 1, 2, 3, 4.

items.narration: Pip is on stone 8. What number comes next? Is it 9, 6, or 10?
items.why: After 8 comes 9. Count one more: 8, 9.

items.narration: Count the frogs. How many frogs are there?
items.why: Touch each frog and count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. There are 5.

items.narration: Count with Pip. 4, 5, 6. What number comes next?
items.why: After 6 comes 7. We count by ones: 4, 5, 6, 7.

items.narration: Hop Pip to the number 3.
items.why: Count the hops from 0: 1, 2, 3. Pip lands on 3.

items.narration: Count with Pip. 11, 12, 13. What comes next? Is it 14, 15, or 12?
items.why: After 13 comes 14. Count one more each time.

items.narration: What number comes after 16? Is it 15, 18, 17, or 13?
items.why: We count 16, 17. The number after 16 is 17.

items.narration: Pip is on stone 12. Which number does he hop to next?
items.why: After 12 comes 13. Count one more: 12, 13.

items.narration: Pip is on 11. Hop him one more, to the next number.
items.why: After 11 comes 12. Pip hops one stone to 12.

items.narration: Count 13, 14. Hop Pip to the next number.
items.why: After 14 comes 15. Count 13, 14, 15.

items.narration: Count with Pip. 17, 18, 19. What comes next? Is it 20, 16, or 19?
items.why: After 19 comes 20. Pip counted all the way to 20!

items.narration: Count with Pip. 18, 19. What number comes next?
items.why: After 19 comes 20. Count one more: 18, 19, 20.

items.narration: Count the stars. How many stars are there?
items.why: Touch each star and count by ones. The last number is 14.

items.narration: Pip is on 17. Hop 3 more. Count 18, 19, 20. Where does he land?
items.why: Hop one at a time: 18, 19, 20. Pip lands on 20.

items.narration: Start at 14. Count 15, 16, 17. Hop Pip to the last number.
items.why: Count by ones: 15, 16, 17. The last number is 17.

items.narration: Mia has 4 cats. The number 4 is used for what? Is it how many, or a name?
items.why: Mia counts 4 cats. The number tells how many cats there are.

items.narration: Count the stars. How many stars are there?
items.why: Touch each star and count. The last number you reach is how many.

items.narration: Mia has 5 balloons. Hop the frog to 5.
items.why: Mia has 5 balloons. Count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 along the line.

items.narration: Ben's shirt has the number 7. The 7 is his player number. Is it a name, or how many?
items.why: A player number is like a name. It does not count anything.

items.narration: Here are some fish. How many fish do you count?
items.why: Count each fish one time. The last number is how many fish.

items.narration: Sam is first in line. Does first mean how many, which one, or a name?
items.why: First tells the place in line. It tells which one Sam is.

items.narration: Sam has 8 balls. Hop the frog to the number that tells how many.
items.why: Sam has 8 balls. Hop to 8 on the line.

items.narration: Which one uses a number for how many? Is it 6 hats, or bus number 6?
items.why: 6 hats is a group we can count. Bus number 6 is just a name.

items.narration: Five ducks stand in a line. The first duck is in place 1. What place is the last duck in? Type its place number.
items.why: Count the ducks in line. The last duck matches that count.

items.narration: A frog is third in line. Hop the frog to 3.
items.why: First is 1, second is 2, and third is 3. Hop to 3.

items.narration: Jo's door has the number 12 on it. Is the 12 how many, which one, or a name?
items.why: The 12 on a door names the home. It does not count things.

items.narration: Jo has some apples. Count them. How many apples does Jo have?
items.why: Count each apple one time. The last number you reach is how many.

items.narration: Ana is seventh in line. Hop the frog to the number for her place.
items.why: Seventh means the place after sixth. Count to 7 and hop there.

items.narration: Which one uses a number as a name? Is it shirt number 8, 8 dogs, or eighth in line?
items.why: Shirt number 8 names a player. 8 dogs counts, and eighth gives a place.

items.narration: The cat is second in line. Is the cat's place 4, 1, 3, or 2?
items.why: First is 1. Second comes next, so second is 2.

items.narration: Look fast! How many ladybugs do you see? Is it 1, 2, or 3?
items.why: There are 2 ladybugs. Look at them together. You can see 2 at once.

items.narration: Look fast! How many stars do you see?
items.why: There are 3 stars. Three is a small group. You can see it at once.

items.narration: Mia sees 1 dot on a card. Hop the frog to 1.
items.why: Mia sees 1 dot. So the frog hops to 1 on the line.

items.narration: Look fast! How many dots are in the ten-frame? Is it 3, 4, or 5?
items.why: There are 3 dots. Look at them together. You do not need to count.

items.narration: Look fast! How many apples do you see?
items.why: There are 2 apples. Two is a small group. You can see it at once.

items.narration: Look fast! How many fish do you see? Is it 3, 4, or 5?
items.why: There are 4 fish. Think of two and two. That makes 4.

items.narration: Look fast! How many dots are in the ten-frame?
items.why: There are 4 dots. Two and two make 4. You can see it at once.

items.narration: Sam sees 4 dots on a card. Hop the frog to 4.
items.why: Sam sees 4 dots. So the frog hops to 4 on the line.

items.narration: Look fast! How many stars are there? Is it 4, 5, or 3?
items.why: There are 5 stars. Five is one full row of the ten-frame.

items.narration: Look fast! How many frogs do you see?
items.why: There are 3 frogs. Look at them together. Three is quick to see.

items.narration: Look fast! How many dots are in the ten-frame? Is it 2, 4, or 5?
items.why: There are 5 dots. They fill one whole row. That row is 5.

items.narration: Look fast! How many strawberries do you see?
items.why: There are 5 strawberries. Try seeing 3 and 2 together. That makes 5.

items.narration: Max sees 2 red dots and 3 blue dots. How many dots in all? Hop the frog there.
items.why: Two dots and three dots make 5 dots. So the frog hops to 5.

items.narration: Ben sees 2 dots, then 2 more dots. Look fast! How many dots in all? Is it 3, 4, or 5?
items.why: Two dots and two more dots make 4. You can see 4 at once.

items.narration: Look very fast! How many butterflies do you see?
items.why: There are 4 butterflies. See two and two together. That makes 4.

items.narration: Count the fish. How many fish are there? Is it 3, 4, or 5?
items.why: Touch each fish and count. 1, 2, 3, 4. There are 4 fish.

items.narration: Pip has some apples. Count them. Type how many apples.
items.why: Count each apple one by one. 1, 2. There are 2 apples.

items.narration: Help Pip hop. Move the frog to the number 6.
items.why: Count along the line. 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Stop at 6.

items.narration: Look at the dots in the box. How many dots? Is it 6, 5, or 4?
items.why: Count the dots one by one. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. There are 5 dots.

items.narration: Here is one frog. Type the number of frogs.
items.why: There is just one frog. One is written as 1.

items.narration: Pip sees stars. How many stars are there? Is it 8, 9, or 10?
items.why: Count each star one time. You get to 9. There are 9 stars.

items.narration: Count the dots in the box. Type how many dots.
items.why: Count the dots one by one. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. There are 7.

items.narration: Pip hops by 2s. Move the frog to the number 12.
The box has no dots. What number is that? Is it 1, 0, or 10?
items.why: There are no dots at all. No dots is the number 0.

items.narration: Pip found ladybugs. Count them. Type how many ladybugs.
items.why: Count each bug one time. You get to 11. There are 11 ladybugs.

items.narration: Pip has balloons. How many balloons are there? Is it 14, 15, or 16?
items.why: Count the balloons one by one. After 14 comes 15. There are 15.

items.narration: Pip picked strawberries. Count them all. Type how many strawberries.
items.why: Count each one time. Go slowly up to 18. There are 18.

items.narration: Help Pip hop far. Move the frog to the number 17.
items.why: Count along the line. Go past 10, 11, 12, up to 17. Stop at 17.

items.narration: Pip wants the number 13. Which number is 13? Is it 31, 3, or 13?
items.why: The number 13 has a 1 first, then a 3. It is 13.

items.narration: Pip has lots of flowers. Count them all. Type how many flowers.
items.why: Count each flower one time. Keep going to 20. There are 20 flowers.

items.narration: Pip counts up from 4 to 5. Is the number bigger or smaller?
items.why: Counting up makes the number bigger. 5 is bigger than 4.

items.narration: Count up from 6. What number comes next?
items.why: When we count up, we go to the next number. After 6 comes 7.

items.narration: Pip starts at 4. Count up one. Hop the frog to that number.
items.why: Counting up one from 4 lands on 5.

items.narration: Pip has 5 blocks. Pip takes one away. Is the number bigger or smaller now?
items.why: Counting down makes the number smaller. 4 is smaller than 5.

items.narration: Count down from 5. What number comes next?
items.why: When we count down, the number gets smaller. Just before 5 is 4.

items.narration: Pip starts at 8. Count down one. Hop the frog to that number.
items.why: Counting down one from 8 lands on 7.

items.narration: Pip hops from 9 to 8. Is that counting up or counting down?
items.why: 8 is smaller than 9. The number got smaller, so Pip counted down.

items.narration: Count up from 9. What number comes next?
items.why: Counting up gives a bigger number. After 9 comes 10.

items.narration: Count down from 7. Which number comes next, 8, 6, or 9?
items.why: Counting down makes the number smaller. Just before 7 is 6.

items.narration: Pip starts at 5. Count up 2 hops. Hop the frog to where Pip lands.
items.why: From 5, count up: 6, then 7. Pip lands on 7.

items.narration: Pip starts at 4. Count up 3 hops. Where does Pip land?
items.why: From 4, count up: 5, 6, then 7. Pip lands on 7.

items.narration: Pip has 6 blocks. Pip adds 2 more. Are there more or fewer blocks now?
items.why: Adding is like counting up. The number gets bigger, so there are more blocks.

items.narration: Pip starts at 9. Count down 3 hops. Hop the frog to where Pip lands.
items.why: From 9, count down: 8, 7, then 6. Pip lands on 6.

items.narration: Here are 5 blocks. Pip takes 2 away. How many blocks are left?
items.why: Count down from 5: 4, then 3. There are 3 blocks left.

items.narration: Pip starts at 3 and ends at 7. Did Pip count up or count down?
items.why: 7 is bigger than 3. The number got bigger, so Pip counted up.

items.narration: Which group has more, 2 stars or 7 stars?
items.why: 7 stars is a bigger group than 2 stars. So 7 stars has more.

items.narration: Which group has less, 6 dogs or 3 dogs?
items.why: 3 dogs is a smaller group than 6 dogs. So 3 dogs has less.

items.narration: Which number is more, 4 or 9? Type the bigger number.
items.why: 9 comes after 4 when we count. So 9 is more than 4.

items.narration: Hop the frog to 1 more than 4.
items.why: Count 4, then 5. One more than 4 is 5.

items.narration: Pip has 4 apples. Mia has 4 apples. Is it more, less, or the same?
items.why: Both have 4. When two groups match, they are the same.

items.narration: Which group has more, 8 hearts or 9 hearts?
items.why: Count up: 8, then 9. 9 comes later, so 9 hearts has more.

items.narration: Pip has 7 apples. Mia has 5 apples. Does Pip have more, less, or the same?
items.why: 7 is a bigger group than 5. So Pip has more.

items.narration: Pip has 6 apples. Mia has 1 more than Pip. How many does Mia have?
items.why: Start at 6 and count one more. 7! Mia has 7.

items.narration: Hop the frog to 2 less than 8.
items.why: Count back from 8. 7, then 6. Two less than 8 is 6.

items.narration: Which number is less, 7 or 2? Type the smaller number.
items.why: 2 comes before 7 when we count. So 2 is less than 7.

items.narration: This ten-frame shows 9. Another has 10. Is 9 more, less, or the same?
items.why: 9 is one dot short of a full ten-frame. So 9 is less than 10.

items.narration: Here are 6 apples. Which group has the same, 5 stars, 6 stars, or 7 stars?
items.why: Match each apple with a star. 6 stars matches 6 apples, so it is the same.

items.narration: Tom has 8 cars. Sam has 5 cars. How many more cars does Tom have?
items.why: Match 5 cars with 5 cars. Then count the extra ones: 3. Tom has 3 more.

items.narration: Hop the frog to 3 more than 6.
items.why: Count up from 6: 7, 8, 9. Three more than 6 is 9.

items.narration: Pip has 10 apples. Mia has 3 fewer. Hop the frog to how many Mia has.
items.why: Count back from 10: 9, 8, 7. Mia has 7 apples.

items.narration: Which number is greater, 3 or 6?
items.why: 6 is more than 3. Count up from 3 and you reach 6. So 6 is greater.

items.narration: Pip has 4 apples. What is 1 more than 4?
items.why: Count up one from 4. 4, then 5. So 1 more than 4 is 5.

items.narration: Move the frog to 1 more than 5.
items.why: Start at 5. Hop up one step. You land on 6.

items.narration: Which number is less, 8 or 2?
items.why: 2 is fewer than 8. Count up from 2 and you reach 8 much later. So 2 is less.

items.narration: What is 1 less than 3?
items.why: Count down one from 3. 3, then 2. So 1 less than 3 is 2.

items.narration: Which number is greater, 9 or 12?
items.why: 12 comes after 9 when we count. Numbers that come later are greater. So 12 is greater.

items.narration: Pip has 6 apples and finds 2 more. What is 2 more than 6?
items.why: Count up two from 6. 7, then 8. So 2 more than 6 is 8.

items.narration: Move the frog to 2 less than 9.
items.why: Start at 9. Hop back two steps. 8, then 7. You land on 7.

items.narration: What is 1 less than 10? Is it 9, 11, or 8?
items.why: Less means count down. One step down from 10 is 9.

items.narration: What is 2 less than 11?
items.why: Count down two from 11. 10, then 9. So 2 less than 11 is 9.

items.narration: Which number is less, 14 or 16?
items.why: Count up: 14, 15, 16. 14 comes first, so 14 is less.

items.narration: Move the frog to 2 more than 15.
items.why: Start at 15. Hop up two steps. 16, then 17. You land on 17.

items.narration: What is 2 more than 18?
items.why: Count up two from 18. 19, then 20. So 2 more than 18 is 20.

items.narration: Which number is 2 less than 13? Is it 11, 12, or 14?
items.why: Count down two from 13. 12, then 11. So 11 is 2 less.

items.narration: Move the frog to 1 less than 17.
items.why: Start at 17. Hop back one step. You land on 16.

items.narration: Here are 5 apples. 3 are red and 2 are green. 3 and 2 make what? Is it 4, 5, or 6?
items.why: Put 3 and 2 together. Count on: 3, then 4, 5. It makes 5.

items.narration: Here are 5 bugs. 4 are on a leaf. How many are not on the leaf?
items.why: 5 bugs in all. 4 are on the leaf. Just 1 bug is left over.

items.narration: Lola has 4 hats in all. 1 hat is red. The rest are blue. Hop to how many are blue.
items.why: 4 hats in all. Take away the 1 red hat. 3 blue hats are left.

items.narration: Here are 4 berries. 2 and 2 make what? Is it 5, 3, or 4?
items.why: Put 2 and 2 together. Count on: 2, then 3, 4. It makes 4.

items.narration: Max has 3 red cars and 3 blue cars. How many cars in all?
items.why: Put the 3 red cars with the 3 blue cars. Count them all. There are 6.

items.narration: Here are 6 apples. 6 is 4 and what? Is it 2, 3, or 4?
items.why: Start at 4. Count up to 6: 5, 6. That is 2 more.

items.narration: Sam has 8 coins. 5 coins are in a jar. Hop to how many are out of the jar.
items.why: 8 coins in all. 5 are in the jar. Count up from 5 to 8. That is 3.

items.narration: Here is a ten frame with 7 dots. 7 is 5 and what? Type the missing part.
items.why: A full row has 5 dots. Count the dots left in the next row. There are 2.

items.narration: Which pair makes 8? Is it 5 and 2, 4 and 3, or 5 and 3?
items.why: Add each pair. 5 and 3 make 8. The other pairs make 7.

items.narration: Ana has 9 stickers. 5 are stars. The rest are hearts. Hop to how many are hearts.
items.why: 9 stickers in all. 5 are stars. Count up from 5 to 9. That is 4 hearts.

items.narration: Here is a ten frame with 6 dots. How many more dots make 10?
items.why: A full ten frame has 10 dots. Count the empty spots. There are 4.

items.narration: Which pair makes 10? Is it 6 and 5, 7 and 2, or 7 and 3?
items.why: Add each pair. 7 and 3 make 10. The other pairs do not.

items.narration: Tom has 10 grapes. 7 grapes are in a bowl. Hop to how many are not in the bowl.
items.why: 10 grapes in all. 7 are in the bowl. Count up from 7 to 10. That is 3.

items.narration: Here are 9 blocks. 9 is made of 2 and a missing part. What is the missing part?
items.why: Start at 2. Count up to 9. That is 7 more.

items.narration: Pip has 8 flies. 6 are on a rock. The rest are on a log. How many are on the log? Is it 3, 4, 1, or 2?
items.why: 8 flies in all. 6 are on the rock. Count up from 6 to 8. That is 2.

items.narration: Pip has 2 apples. 1 more apple comes. How many apples now? Is it 3, 2, or 4?
items.why: Start with 2 apples. Add 1 more. Count on: 2, then 3. The answer is 3.

items.narration: Pip sees 2 bugs. 1 more bug comes. How many bugs in all?
items.why: Count the 2 bugs. Then count 1 more. That makes 3 bugs.

items.narration: Pip has 2 fish. 2 more fish swim in. Hop the frog to how many fish.
items.why: Start at 2. Hop 2 more steps. You land on 4.

items.narration: Pip has 3 cookies. Pip eats 1. How many cookies are left? Is it 2, 1, or 3?
items.why: Start with 3 cookies. Take away 1. Count back: 3, then 2. So 2 are left.

items.narration: There are 3 birds. 1 bird flies away. How many birds are left?
items.why: Start with 3 birds. Take away 1. That leaves 2 birds.

items.narration: 2 and 3 make how many? Is it 4, 6, or 5?
items.why: Start at 3. Count on 2 more: 4, 5. So 2 and 3 make 5.

items.narration: Pip has 5 stars. 3 stars go away. Hop the frog to how many are left.
items.why: Start at 5. Hop back 3 steps: 4, 3, 2. You land on 2.

items.narration: What is 4 + 1?
items.why: One more than 4 is 5. So 4 + 1 = 5.

items.narration: What is 5 - 2? Is it 3, 2, or 4?
items.why: Start at 5. Count back 2: 4, 3. The answer is 3.

items.narration: 3 frogs sit on a log. 2 more frogs hop on. Hop to how many frogs in all.
items.why: Start at 3. Hop 2 more: 4, 5. You land on 5.

items.narration: Pip wants 5 bugs. Pip has 2 bugs. How many more bugs does Pip need?
items.why: Start at 2. Count up to 5: 3, 4, 5. That is 3 more.

items.narration: Which pair makes 5? Is it 1 and 3, 2 and 3, or 4 and 2?
items.why: Add each pair. 1 and 3 make 4. 2 and 3 make 5. 4 and 2 make 6.

items.narration: Pip has 4 apples. Pip eats 3. Hop the frog to how many are left.
items.why: Start at 4. Hop back 3 steps: 3, 2, 1. You land on 1.

items.narration: Pip has 5 pears. Pip eats all 5. How many pears are left?
items.why: Take away all 5 pears. Nothing is left. The answer is 0.

items.narration: Here are 3 dots. Add 2 more dots. How many dots now? Is it 5, 4, or 3?
items.why: Start with 3 dots. Add 2 more: 4, 5. Now there are 5 dots.

items.narration: Tom has 2 cats. 1 more cat comes. How many cats now? Is it 2, 3, or 4?
items.why: Start with 2 cats. Add 1 more. Count on: 3.

items.narration: Pip has 4 fish. 1 fish swims away. How many fish are left?
items.why: Start with 4 fish. Take away 1. Count back: 3.

items.narration: Mia has 3 apples. She gets 2 more. Hop the frog to how many apples she has.
items.why: Start at 3. Hop 2 more: 4, 5. Mia has 5.

items.narration: Sam has 5 balloons. 2 balloons pop. How many are left? Is it 4, 2, or 3?
items.why: Start with 5. Take away 2. Count back: 4, 3. Sam has 3.

items.narration: 2 birds sit on a branch. 2 more birds come. How many birds now?
items.why: Hold up 2 fingers. Then 2 more. Count them all: 4.

items.narration: Lily has 6 stars. She gets 3 more. Hop the frog to how many stars she has.
items.why: Start at 6. Count on 3: 7, 8, 9. Lily has 9.

items.narration: Max has 9 cookies. He eats 4. How many cookies are left?
items.why: Start at 9. Count back 4: 8, 7, 6, 5. Max has 5.

items.narration: Ana has 7 balloons. 5 are red. The rest are blue. How many are blue? Is it 2, 3, or 1?
items.why: Take the 5 red away from 7. Count what is left: 2 blue.

items.narration: Ben has 8 grapes. Zoe has 5 grapes. How many more does Ben have? Is it 2, 4, or 3?
items.why: Match each of Zoe's grapes to one of Ben's. Ben has 3 left over.

items.narration: Leo has 10 stickers. He gives 4 away. Hop the frog to how many stickers he has now.
items.why: Start at 10. Count back 4: 9, 8, 7, 6. Leo has 6.

items.narration: Kim has 6 shells. She finds 4 more. How many shells does she have?
items.why: Start at 6. Count on 4: 7, 8, 9, 10. Kim has 10.

items.narration: There are 10 ducks. 6 are in the pond. The rest are on the grass. How many are on the grass? Is it 3, 5, 6, or 4?
items.why: Take the 6 pond ducks away from 10. Count back: 4 ducks on the grass.

items.narration: Dan has 9 cars. Eve has 4 cars. How many more cars does Dan have?
items.why: Match 4 cars to 4 cars. Count Dan's extra cars: 5.

items.narration: Tom has 5 apples. He gets 3 more. Then he eats 2. Hop the frog to how many apples Tom has.
items.why: 5 and 3 more makes 8. Then take away 2. Tom has 6.

items.narration: Jo has 3 hats. Ali has 7 hats. How many fewer hats does Jo have? Is it 3, 4, 5, or 10?
items.why: Match 3 hats to 3 hats. Ali has 4 extra. So Jo has 4 fewer.

items.narration: Mia gets 2 cookies. Sam gets 2 cookies. Is it fair? Yes or no?
items.why: Mia has 2 and Sam has 2. They have the same, so it is fair.

items.narration: There are 2 apples and 2 friends. Each friend gets the same. How many apples does each get?
items.why: Give one apple to each friend. Then no apples are left. Each friend gets 1.

items.narration: 4 ducks swim to 2 ponds. Each pond gets the same. Hop the frog to how many ducks each pond gets.
items.why: Put one duck in each pond. Then one more each.

items.narration: There are 4 stickers and 4 friends. Each friend gets the same. How many stickers does each get? 1, 2, or 4?
items.why: There is one sticker for each friend. Each friend gets 1 sticker.

items.narration: Sam has 6 cookies. He shares them with 2 friends. How many cookies does each friend get?
items.why: Hand out one cookie at a time to each friend. Each friend ends up with 3.

items.narration: Lily has 6 berries. She shares them with 3 friends. How many berries does each friend get? 2, 3, or 4?
items.why: Give each friend one berry. Then give another to each.

items.narration: Max has 8 toy cars. He shares them with 2 friends. How many cars does each friend get?
items.why: Give each friend one car at a time. Each friend gets 4.

items.narration: 9 grapes are shared by 3 friends. Hop the frog to how many grapes each friend gets.
items.why: Give 3 friends one grape each, three times. Each friend gets 3 grapes.

items.narration: Ana gets 4 cookies. Ben gets 2 cookies. Is it fair? Yes or no?
items.why: Ana has more than Ben. They need the same amount, so it is not fair.

items.narration: There are 10 stars. 2 friends share them equally. How many stars does each friend get?
items.why: Give one star to each friend, again and again. Each friend gets 5.

items.narration: Zoe has 8 pencils. She shares them with 4 friends. How many pencils does each friend get? 1, 2, 3, or 4?
items.why: Give 4 friends one pencil each. That uses 4. Give one more each. Each friend gets 2.

items.narration: There are 9 apples. 3 friends share them equally. How many apples does each friend get?
items.why: Give each friend one apple, three times. All 9 are shared. Each friend gets 3.

items.narration: 10 balloons are shared by 5 friends. Hop the frog to how many balloons each friend gets.
items.why: Give 5 friends one balloon each. Then give one more each. Each friend gets 2.

items.narration: 4 friends each get 2 cookies. All the cookies were shared equally. How many cookies were there?
items.why: Count 2 for each friend. 2 and 2 and 2 and 2 is 8.

items.narration: There are 6 cookies for 2 friends. Which way shares them equally? 4 and 2, 3 and 3, or 5 and 1?
items.why: Equal means the same number each. 3 and 3 is the same, and it makes 6.
